   Local News Federal Inmate Receives Additional Sentence In Drug Smuggling Scheme
 Nov 10, 2026 A federal inmate has been sentenced to an additional two-years in prison for conspiring to smuggle synthetic drugs into the Wyatt Detention Facility. 
 According to the U.S. Attorney's Office of Rhode Island, 34-year-old Randy Diaz-Pizarro teamed up with another inmate, a facility employee and a person on the outside to bring drug-soaked paper into the facility. 
 Federal prosecutors say Diaz-Pizarro coordinated payments and communications for the scheme. 
 "Correctional facilities cannot operate safely when inmates and their associates attempt to turn them into marketplaces for illegal drugs," said First Assistant United States Attorney Charles C. Calenda. “This type of criminal conduct undermines the safety and security of these institutions and puts both staff and inmates at risk. A prison sentence is not an opportunity to continue criminal activity, and those who do so risk adding years to their incarceration.” 
 “Randy Diaz-Pizarro is an unrepentant career criminal who smuggled drug-soaked papers into a detention center not only for his own use, but for his fellow inmates to purchase. His blatant disregard of the law undermined the safety of this facility,” said Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s (FBI) Boston Division. “This sentence should serve as a warning: the FBI and our partners are working every day to identify and bring to justice those who seek to profit from criminal activity while behind bars.”
 The new sentence will be served consecutive to the 120-month sentence he is currently serving on a conviction in Massachusetts.
